ideas.pitch: A co-op debugging terminal where three players take distinct roles with fragmented system telemetry to fix a simulated server crash under time pressure.
ideas.problem_statement: Round 2 takes you into a set of technical challenges where things aren't always as they seem. You have to explore the system, find clues and figure out what went wrong.
ideas.title: Asymmetric SysAdmin
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly matches the event's core premise of asymmetric information sharing and technical system exploration, leveraging a working live demo of multi-user terminal synchronization.

ideas.pitch: A multi-player command line decryption game where each team member possesses only one-third of the encryption keys and must verbally coordinate to prevent a simulated data wipe.
ideas.problem_statement: Round 1 puts your team’s communication to the test. Each person has a different role and access to different information. You will have to rely on each other to understand the clues and move forward.
ideas.title: Protocol Broken
ideas.why_it_could_win: Focuses intensely on communication mechanics and rapid trust-building, perfectly fitting the mandatory team-sync format of the first challenge round.

ideas.pitch: An interactive hardware-software hybrid puzzle box where players must physically plug components into an ESP32 board while communicating circuit states across distributed browser views.
ideas.problem_statement: Round 2 takes you into a set of technical challenges where things aren't always as they seem. You will have to explore the system, find clues and figure out what went wrong.
ideas.title: Silent Circuit
ideas.why_it_could_win: Brings physical hardware into a room likely dominated by pure software applications, instantly standing out to judges through a tangible working prototype.

ideas.pitch: A collaborative log-analysis interface that deliberately fragments error traces across three distinct dashboard views, requiring all three team members to cross-reference logs to find the root vulnerability.
ideas.problem_statement: Each person has a different role and access to different information. You will have to rely on each other to understand the clues and move forward.
ideas.title: LogSplit
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solvers will love the practical application of developer toolings combined with high-stakes communication bottlenecks.

ideas.pitch: A network routing packet game where players act as different OSI layers, seeing only their designated layer's headers and collaborating to route a corrupted payload through a live proxy.
ideas.problem_statement: One wrong message can change everything. You have to think fast, communicate better and importantly trust your team.
ideas.title: Blind Trust Router
ideas.why_it_could_win: Employs genuinely hard networking and state-sync engineering while perfectly mapping to the event's strict three-player team constraint.
